table.name: flyway_schema_history
table.remarks: NOT A FLYWAY TABLE, AND THIS IS NOT A FLYWAY REPOSITORY. It is a view over knex_migrations created by migrations/20241120000001_form_db.js purely so tooling that expects Flyway keeps working - specifically the HMPPS subject access request test support library, which asserts an expected schema version. This repository uses knex; schema changes belong in migrations/. Running Flyway against this database will collide with this view.

column.name: version
column.remarks: The knex migration filename, presented as if it were a Flyway version. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: knex_migrations
table.remarks: Knex's own record of which migrations have been applied. Not part of the use of force domain schema.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: name
column.remarks: Migration filename as it appears in migrations/. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: batch
column.remarks: Which batch the migration was applied in; a batch is one run of migrate.latest(). [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: migration_time
column.remarks: When the migration was applied. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: knex_migrations_lock
table.remarks: Knex's advisory lock, preventing two instances migrating at once. Migrations run at application boot, so every pod attempts them on start.

column.name: index
column.remarks: Primary key. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: is_locked
column.remarks: Non-zero while a migration run holds the lock. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: report
table.remarks: One use of force incident report. Nothing is ever hard-deleted: "deleted" is a timestamp tombstone, and the application reads and writes through the v_report view. A draft is simply a row with status IN_PROGRESS - there is no separate draft table. The table has no outbound foreign keys and its primary key constraint is still named pk_form, from when the table was called "form".

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. The sequence is still named form_id_seq after the original table name. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: form_response
column.remarks: The entire report as submitted, as JSON. Holds the reasons force was used, the techniques and restraint positions applied, what was observed, and the relocationAndInjuries section - which records prisoner injuries, hospitalisation, healthcare involvement, the healthcare practitioner's name and whether staff needed medical attention. Health data about both the prisoner and staff. See docs/report-payload.md for the shape, and reference-data.csv for the permitted values. [Sensitivity: SPECIAL-CATEGORY]

column.name: user_id
column.remarks: HMPPS username of the officer who created the report. Nullable in the database - a 2019 migration altered the column and dropped the not-null constraint - but always populated in practice. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: sequence_no
column.remarks: Distinguishes multiple reports by the same officer against the same booking. Computed as MAX(sequence_no) + 1 for that user and booking. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: booking_id
column.remarks: NOMIS booking id: the custody period of the prisoner force was used on. Defaults to -1 where unknown. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: created_date
column.remarks: When the report was created. Originally named start_date. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: status
column.remarks: IN_PROGRESS, SUBMITTED or COMPLETE. No check constraint - the application enforces it. See reference-data.csv. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: submitted_date
column.remarks: When the reporting officer submitted the report, which is what creates the statement rows. Null while still a draft. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: offender_no
column.remarks: NOMIS offender number of the prisoner force was used on. The identifier that makes every row in this schema personal data about that prisoner. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: reporter_name
column.remarks: Display name of the reporting officer, captured at creation so the report reads correctly even after the officer leaves. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: incident_date
column.remarks: When force was used. Extracted out of form_response into its own column so it can be indexed and searched. Places a named prisoner at a point in time. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: agency_id
column.remarks: Prison the incident happened at, as a NOMIS agency code such as MDI. Stamped at creation and updatable through the change-prison flow. With incident_date, locates a named prisoner. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: updated_date
column.remarks: When the report was last changed. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: deleted
column.remarks: Soft-delete tombstone. Non-null rows are filtered out by the v_report view; nothing is physically removed. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: completed_date
column.remarks: Intended to record when every required statement had been submitted. Added October 2025 and not yet written or read by anything - do not rely on it. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: report_edit
table.remarks: History of post-submission edits made through the coordinator edit flow. Its primary key constraint is named pk_edit. As with report_log, report_id has NO foreign key to report, so edit history survives a soft-delete and SchemaSpy draws no relationship line.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: edit_date
column.remarks: When the edit was made. Originally named timestamp. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: editor_user_id
column.remarks: HMPPS username of the coordinator who made the edit. Originally named user_id. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: editor_name
column.remarks: Display name of that coordinator. Originally named user_name. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: report_id
column.remarks: The report that was edited. Not a declared foreign key - see the table comment. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: reason
column.remarks: Coded reason for the edit, covering the edit, add-staff, remove-staff and delete-report journeys. See reference-data.csv for the permitted values. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: additional_comments
column.remarks: Free text from the coordinator expanding on the edit. Not a health or offence question in itself, but free text about a named prisoner's report and capable of carrying that detail. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: report_owner_changed
column.remarks: Whether this edit reassigned the report to a different reporting officer. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: changes
column.remarks: What the edit changed, as JSON keyed by field, each entry holding oldValue, newValue and the question text. Contains arbitrary before and after slices of the report, including involved staff and the relocation and injuries answers. See docs/report-payload.md. [Sensitivity: SPECIAL-CATEGORY]

column.name: reason_text
column.remarks: Free text supplied when the coded reason is "another reason". Same caveat as additional_comments. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

table.name: report_log
table.remarks: Audit trail of what happened to a report. Its primary key constraint is named pk_audit. report_id is a plain bigint with NO foreign key to report, deliberately, so audit rows survive the report being soft-deleted - which is why SchemaSpy draws this table with no relationship line to report.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: timestamp
column.remarks: When the action happened. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: username
column.remarks: HMPPS username of the person who acted, or the literal SYSTEM for automatic status transitions. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: report_id
column.remarks: The report acted on. Not a declared foreign key - see the table comment. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: action
column.remarks: What happened: REPORT_CREATED, REPORT_MODIFIED, REPORT_DELETED, REPORT_SUBMITTED, REPORT_STATUS_CHANGED or REPORT_COMPLETED. See reference-data.csv. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: details
column.remarks: Context for the action, as JSON. For REPORT_MODIFIED this holds originalSection and updatedSection - whole before and after slices of report.form_response - so it carries the same incident, injury and healthcare content as the report itself. [Sensitivity: SPECIAL-CATEGORY]

table.name: statement
table.remarks: One member of staff's account of a use of force incident, created for each involved officer when the report is submitted. Originally called involved_staff, which still shows in its index names. Read and written through the v_statement view.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. The sequence is still named involved_staff_id_seq after the original table name. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: report_id
column.remarks: The report this statement belongs to. Foreign key to report(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: user_id
column.remarks: HMPPS username of the officer the statement is required from. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: name
column.remarks: Display name of that officer. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: email
column.remarks: Email address used to send statement reminders. May be backfilled later by the reminder job rather than set at creation. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: submitted_date
column.remarks: When the officer submitted their statement. Null while still outstanding. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: statement_status
column.remarks: PENDING or SUBMITTED. See reference-data.csv. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: last_training_month
column.remarks: Month of the officer's most recent control and restraint training, as a ZERO-BASED index: 0 is January and 11 is December, not 1 to 12. Employment record data. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: last_training_year
column.remarks: Year of the officer's most recent control and restraint training. Employment record data. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: job_start_year
column.remarks: Year the officer started in the role. Employment record data. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: statement
column.remarks: The officer's free-text account of the force used on a named prisoner. Routinely records injuries and the healthcare given (Article 9 health data) and describes conduct that may become a criminal or disciplinary allegation against the prisoner or the officer (Article 10). [Sensitivity: SPECIAL-CATEGORY]

column.name: staff_id
column.remarks: NOMIS staff id of the officer. Originally not-null with a -1 default; a 2019 migration made it nullable and dropped the default. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: created_date
column.remarks: When the statement row was created, which is when the report was submitted. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: updated_date
column.remarks: When the statement was last changed. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: next_reminder_date
column.remarks: When the reminder job should next chase this statement. Set to submission plus one day, advanced daily, and nulled once the statement is overdue. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: overdue_date
column.remarks: When the statement becomes overdue - submission plus three days. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: in_progress
column.remarks: Whether the officer has saved a draft of their statement without submitting it. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: deleted
column.remarks: Soft-delete tombstone. Non-null rows are filtered out by the v_statement view. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: removal_requested_reason
column.remarks: Free text written by the member of staff themselves, asking to be removed from the report because they were not involved. Tagged STAFF because it is their own account of their own involvement, but it is free text and can carry health or personal-circumstance detail - handle it with the same care as a special category column. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: removal_requested_date
column.remarks: When removal from the report was requested. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: statement_amendments
table.remarks: Additional comments added by a member of staff after their statement was submitted. A statement is never edited in place; corrections are appended here. Read and written through the v_statement_amendments view.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: statement_id
column.remarks: The statement being amended. Foreign key to statement(id) with ON DELETE CASCADE. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: additional_comment
column.remarks: Free-text addition to a submitted statement. Same content and the same risks as statement.statement - an account of force used on a named prisoner, including injuries and healthcare. [Sensitivity: SPECIAL-CATEGORY]

column.name: date_submitted
column.remarks: When the amendment was submitted. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: deleted
column.remarks: Soft-delete tombstone. Non-null rows are filtered out by the v_statement_amendments view. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: v_report
table.remarks: Live reports: report filtered to deleted IS NULL. The application reads and writes through this view rather than the base table, so a soft-deleted report disappears from the service without being destroyed. It is a simple auto-updatable Postgres view, so UPDATE and INSERT work against it. Columns are as per report.
